title: SLO layering, trace contracts, and dashboard playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook to standardize how we layer SLOs for inference features, define lightweight trace contracts for cross-service correlation, and provide compact dashboard templates for operator and oncall workflows. Focus is on maintaining operational signal fidelity during model rollouts, microburst traffic, and KV-cache warm/cold transitions.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: observability engineers, SREs, serving runtime owners, product leads planning rollouts.
- Scope: production inference pipelines (hosted + dedicated), routing fallback flows, cache/kvcache lifecycle, and model rollout windows. Not a full instrumentation spec; this is the operator-facing plan and checklist.

High-level principles (short):
1) Layer SLOs: user-facing, system-level, and feature-isolation SLOs. Keep user-facing SLOs simple (availability, p50/p95 latencies). System and feature SLOs are for debugging and rollbacks.
2) Trace contracts: traces must carry stable correlation IDs and essential ops fields; keep traces small and privacy-safe.
3) Dashboards: two compact views — Operator (triage-first) and Investigator (drilldown). Avoid >12 panels on operator view.
4) Cost-awareness: prefer aggregated counters and sampled traces; keep query costs bounded.

SLO layering (recommended):
- User-facing SLOs (business):
  - InferenceAvailability: 99.95% 30d (error responses / timeouts for API calls). Owner: hosted-api-product. Metric: ratio of successful responses over attempts across customer endpoints.
  - UserPerceivedLatency_p95: target depends by plan (e.g., 300ms hosted, 150ms dedicated). Tags: plan-tier, region.
- System invariants (engineering):
  - TokenPathTail_99_9: 99.9th percentile of per-token generation latency across token positions. Owner: serving-runtime. Purpose: detect kernel regressions and quantization slowdowns.
  - KVCacheWarmthIndex: fraction of requests served from KV cache for tenant cohorts (0–1). Owner: cache-team. Purpose: detect cold-start regressions after rollout.
- Feature isolation SLOs (debugging):
  - FanoutMultiplierLimit breaches: count of requests that triggered >N model fanouts in a single logical request. Owner: routing. Use for routing rollback triggers.

Metric definitions (compact):
- inference.request.success_rate: numerator: count(status in [200,201]) over window; denominator: total requests. Granularity: 1m. Dimensions: model, route, plan, region, tenant_id_hash.
- inference.response.latency_ms.p95/p99/p999: measured at response completion. Include metadata: prompt_length, completion_length, kv_cache_hit (bool).
- inference.token.latency_ms.quantiles: per-token latency distribution; export histograms at 10ms buckets for quantile estimation.
- kvcache.hit_rate: hits / (hits + misses) for prefix lookup. Buckets by tenant cohort.
- routing.fallback.count: counts where primary model unavailable and fallback path taken.

Trace contract (minimal fields) — keep concise and stable across services:
- trace.trace_id: standard W3C trace id (stable).
- trace.span_id: span id.
- fields (labels) to include on root span: tenant_hash, model_id, model_version, route_id, request_id (short), plan_tier.
- fields on inference span: prompt_tokens, response_tokens, kv_cache_used (true/false), used_quantization_profile, kernel_variant, sequence_length.
- error annotation: error.code (internal), error.class, error.short_msg.
Sampling rules and privacy:
- Default: 0.5% probabilistic sampling for all requests, with adaptive upsampling for errors and high-latency tails.
- Always retain 100% traces for requests that triggered rollback signals or SLO breach within 5m window.
- Redaction: remove PII fields and PRs containing full prompt text from traces by default. If prompt capture is enabled for evals, store prompts only in a separate secure bucket with KMS.

Span size & instrumentation guidelines:
- Keep spans shallow: root -> router -> model-serve -> kv-cache (if used) -> kernel. Avoid per-token span creation unless explicitly for kernel profiling sweeps.
- Use annotations rather than huge attributes; keep attribute count < 20 where possible.

Gateways and cross-service propagation:
- Enrich trace at gateway with tenant_hash and route_id to ensure correlation across routing and serving.
- If request is split (multi-model fanout), include parent_request_id and fanout_index on child spans.

Dashboards (templates and panel list):
Operator view (fast triage, single-screen):
- Top row: Global request rate, error rate, availability SLO burn rate (sparkline).
- Latency row: p50/p95/p99 response latencies by model tier (small stacked bars).
- Cold vs warm: kvcache.hit_rate (global) and KVCacheWarmthIndex by tenant cohort heatmap.
- Tail signals: TokenPathTail_99_9 (single-number alert card) and distribution sparkline.
- Fallbacks & throttles: routing.fallback.count and rate-limit-throttle-rate.
- Quick links: trace search (pre-filled with last 15m high-latency trace filter), playbook link, recent rollouts.
Investigator view (drilldown):
- Time-series: per-model response latencies with annotations for deploys.
- Trace-sampled waterfall: sample traces aligned to latency spikes.
- KVCache flows: histogram of request latency by kv_cache_used=true/false.
- Kernel profiler panel: kernel_variant latency breakdown (for dedicated).
- Cohort panel: per-tenant request costs and token-slope.

Alerting heuristics (suggested):
- Immediate SEV: InferenceAvailability breach > 5min and > 0.5% absolute drop vs baseline.
- Latency SEV: UserPerceivedLatency_p95 exceeds SLO by >2x for 10m.
- Guardrails: KVCacheWarmthIndex drop >20% for top 5 tenants => page SRE oncall, notify product.
- Soft alerts (Slack): small increases in fanout multiplier or sampling anomalies.

Runbook snippets (for the oncall):
1) Check operator dashboard top row. Is overall request rate stable?
2) If availability drop: check routing.fallback.count and region-specific host health.
3) If latency spike but success rate ok: filter traces by highest token-latency contributions, inspect kernel_variant and kvcache_used.
4) If kvcache warmth low: check cache priming jobs, recent model rollout (if rolled in last 30m), and tenant isolation configs.
5) If many fallbacks: confirm model pool capacity and check autoscaler metrics.

Rollout readiness checklist (observability items):
- Do we have pre-rollout baseline snapshots for: p50/p95/p99 and KVCacheWarmthIndex? (Y/N)
- Are trace sampling rates temporarily increased for the rollout window? (Y/N)
- SLO burn rate alert configured and smoke-tested? (Y/N)
- Dashboard bookmarked and team Slack channel pre-warmed? (Y/N)
- Quick rollback play defined (model pin+reroute) with runbook link? (Y/N)

Migration and cost notes:
- Move high-cardinality labels (tenant_id) into a lookup service; use tenant_hash in metrics to bind costs.
- Preserve 90-day coarse-grained aggregates for long-term trend analysis; keep high-resolution for 14d.
- Where possible, emit derived aggregates (e.g., per-model bucketed p99) server-side to avoid expensive query-time group-bys.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we unify token-latency histograms across runtime languages? (needs RFC)
- Is there appetite to capture sampled prompt text for model quality debugging under closed storage? (privacy review required)
- Should we standardize kvcache cohort buckets (auto, warm, cold) across teams? (proposal needed)

Quick references and links:
- CONFLUENCE-OBS-43: SLI/SLO taxonomy (planning page)
- JIRA-OBS-912: Trace-contract enforcement task
- github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/PR-277: instrumentation helpers for kvcache labels

Notes to self (working):
- Try a two-week experiment increasing trace upsample to 5% around controlled rollouts.
- Prototype small operator view that replaces p999 with TailHeat metric to simplify triage.

Sign-off: Asha (owner), to iterate with Miguel and Priya.
